description: BIT* (Batch Informed Trees) joins graph search and random sampling. It treats a batch of random samples as an implicit *random geometric graph* (RGG), in which each sample links to its near neighbours, and searches it like A*: in order of the estimated cost of a solution through each edge, `g + c_hat + h_hat`. It checks an edge for collisions only when that edge comes out on top and can still improve the solution. When no edge can improve the current solution, BIT* removes the states that cannot help, draws a new batch from the *informed set* (the states that can lie on a cheaper path), and searches again while it keeps its tree. It is *anytime*, probabilistically complete and asymptotically optimal: it returns a path early, the path cost never increases, and it converges to the optimum.
